holidays.name: Eat What You Want Day
holidays.description: One glorious day to put down the diet app, ignore the food rules and eat exactly what your heart (and stomach) desires. Dessert first? Breakfast for dinner? Today, nobody can stop you.
holidays.origin: The day was created by Thomas and Ruth Roy of Wellcat Holidays, the couple behind many offbeat food observances. They designed it as a 24-hour break from dieting, calorie counting and guilt.
holidays.funFact: The Roys founded Wellcat Holidays and have registered dozens of quirky celebrations, so this one is part of a much bigger family of oddball days.

holidays.name: Hostess CupCake Day
holidays.description: A salute to the iconic chocolate cupcake with creamy white filling and a squiggly icing swirl on top. Peel the frosting, lick the filling and take a nostalgic bite of lunchbox history.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance honoring the beloved snack cake, which has been a lunchbox staple in America for about a century. The exact origin of the day itself is unclear.
holidays.funFact: The cupcake's signature white squiggle on top is traditionally made up of seven loops, which has made it one of the most recognizable snack designs around.

holidays.name: National Twilight Zone Day
holidays.description: A day for fans of classic television to binge the eerie, mind-bending anthology series that gave us twist endings, haunted airplane wings and a very unfortunate man with a lot of time to read. Pour a drink and enter another dimension.
holidays.origin: An unofficial fan observance celebrating the groundbreaking sci-fi and fantasy series created by Rod Serling. The origin of the date is unclear.
holidays.funFact: The original series ran for five seasons and 156 episodes, and creator Rod Serling wrote or co-wrote a large share of them himself.
